scenes.say: Ever wonder how methods actually change your structs in Go? Let's break down receivers and see why it matters.

scenes.label: Struct
scenes.sub: A group of fields acting as one type.
scenes.say: First, a struct is just a group of fields bundled together, like a mini-record.
Here, GetName uses a value receiver. It works on a copy. SetName uses a pointer receiver, so it can change the real struct.
Value receivers can't change the original struct. Pointer receivers can, and they're also faster for big structs.

scenes.question: Will SetName with value receiver update Name?
scenes.right: No, only pointer receivers update the original struct.
scenes.say: Careful—using a value receiver in SetName won't update your struct. Only pointer receivers do.
